reason: The idea cannot be scored on the LB before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC with P>=0.7 if it keeps its own validation protocol. My estimate is P~0.05-0.08, and the idea as written cannot be built. (1) Missing dependency. The idea is scoped as 'Mode DOGRESCUE_ZSPLIT=1 of the same patch', but tools/dog_rescue.py does not exist in the repo (ls). The dogrescue line was refuted on schedule (P(scored)~0.09, v_localisation-training-free_dog-missing-track-rescue_schedule.json) and on value. So the 'rides in the dogrescue probe' path (earliest probe 28 Sep 10:00) almost certainly has no probe to ride in. Built standalone, it needs its own z-profile, track assembly (Hungarian 4 um, >=6 frames), node cap and insertion: ~3.5-4.5 h of agent work, not 1.5 h. It also needs a new x138 cell-5 patch (build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 supports only divinsert|leafprune, docstring l.13-14): +2-3 h. (2) Lab data. The controls and the increment need raw TRAIN zarr plus final graphs (exp39 tails via replay, or an x138 cache that does not exist yet). Neither is in this container (no data, no Kaggle). Only friend A has both. He has not committed since 24 Sep, he is waiting for #34, and his queued job is the 13-16 GPU-h x138 lab cache. P(he runs controls plus selection/confirmation by Sun 27 ~12:00) ~0.5. (3) Gate. The pre-registered positive/negative control probably passes (v2: distinct 4.5-8 um neighbours have a valley <0.85 in 46% of cases, single GT nuclei q10=1.0; r1_research_hole-fill-sandwich.notes.md), P~0.7. The increment gate over dogrescue is ~0.15-0.25: holes 4-6 um show a valley in only 0-1.2% (<0.85, n=301), and the value verdict gives about +0.0001 central. (4) Kernel, dummy, user OK and slot: ~0.85. Chain: 0.5 x 0.7 x 0.2 x 0.85 ~0.06. (5) Runtime. Cell 5 already has a cached full-res frame reader (blosc2 chunk, used by refine_synthetic_midpoint), so the in-kernel profile is cheap per node. But every frame read in the serial repair loop costs ~0.05-0.1 s x 10-13k hidden frames = ~0.2-0.4 h. That time sits outside the REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=27000 guard (checked per dataset, cell 5 l.2116), so the stage must be deadline-gated or it risks the ~-0.04/movie degradation. A 4-video dummy run cannot detect this. (6) Even when scored, the probe says nothing: the expected +0.0001..+0.0015 is below the 0.003 LB noise. Cited numbers check out (valley stats, ::4 stride, attract3 +0.55..+1.0 um). But attract3 used pairs where both nodes are matched to distinct preds (r2_critic l.18), so it is not evidence of merges.
fix_if_any: Split it into a kill-first desk test and an optional blind rider, and never give it its own slot. (a) Sat 26, ~1 h CPU on friend A's machine, only after his x138-cache job is started: a script (agent, Fri 25 afternoon, ~1.5 h, testable here only on synthetic arrays) computes the z-profile rule on 24 videos (12+12) against exp39 final coords. It reports the control trigger-rate ratio (>=3x), the a_never hits within 3 um of GT, and the false-trigger rate per node. Kill unless the hits extrapolate to >=150 FN over 199 videos in runs of 6 or more at <=0.3% added nodes. (b) Only if (a) passes: a --patch zsplit for --base x138 with ZSPLIT_ENABLE=0 byte-identical. Reuse cell 5's frame reader, skip the stage when kernel elapsed > ~6.0 h, and log per-movie seconds and trigger counts (agent 2-3 h, Sat/Sun). Dummy run on the same day as another x138 probe's dummy run (~0.5-1 GPU-h after the 26 Sep reset). Submit only as a rider on an already-planned x138-based probe, by Mon 28 ~24:00 UTC at the latest. Without friend A, a blind rider is schedulable (P(scored)~0.75) but unvalidated and indistinguishable from noise, so I do not recommend it.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0000..+0.0005 (central ~+0.0001, below the 0.003 LB noise). Downside ~-0.0005 from false splits of z-elongated nuclei. If the stage is left unguarded in the serial repair loop, there is a tail risk of up to ~-0.04 per movie pushed past the 7.5 h degradation line.
realistic_private_gain: +0.0000..+0.0008 (central ~+0.0002). The same false-split and runtime tail risks apply, and both scores come from the same hidden run.
